title: withdraw() silently increases the withdrawal amount when remaining would fall in (0, MINIMUM_STAKE), with no caller-visible warning
rootCause: When the caller requests `amount` such that `0 < user.amount - amount < MINIMUM_STAKE`, the dust handler overrides the requested amount and forces a full withdrawal of `user.amount`. The user receives more than they asked for, and `user.amount` is set to 0, ending their staking position. The only on-chain signal is the `Withdrawn(msg.sender, actualWithdrawAmount)` event, which the user must inspect to learn that the amount changed.
impact: User flow disruption: a wallet/integration calling `withdraw(amount)` expecting a partial cash-out will instead exit the position entirely. Subsequent calls relying on `user.amount > 0` (e.g. zappers, auto-compounders, dollar-cost-averaging scripts) will fail. While the protocol's invariant (`amount = 0` or `amount >= MINIMUM_STAKE`) is preserved by this behavior, the silent override is a UX bug and a minor footgun. Compare to other staking systems which revert with `'amount leaves dust'` and let the caller choose.
attackVector: n/a -- self-inflicted UX issue. Mildly weaponizable: a malicious integrator could craft `amount = user.amount - MINIMUM_STAKE + 1` to grief other users' partial withdrawals through a shared integration -- but the integrator already needs the user's privileges to call `withdraw` on their behalf, so practical impact is low.
steps: user calls withdraw(1.5e15) expecting to leave 0.5e15 staked.
remaining = 0.5e15 > 0 AND remaining < MINIMUM_STAKE (1e15) -> dust handler triggers.
Contract sends 2e15 phUSD to user instead of 1.5e15; position closed.
remediation: Either revert with a clear error (`require(remaining == 0 || remaining >= MINIMUM_STAKE, 'leaves dust')`) so the caller chooses, or emit a dedicated event (`event DustWithdraw(address user, uint256 requested, uint256 actual);`) so off-chain integrators can react. Reverting is the safer default.
profileReference: Profile §4.3 withdraw dust handling 'Downstream UX concern, not a security issue per se.'
